item.title: Qualitative Study Reveals Lack of Consensus on Laboratory Rat Handling Methods
item.description: The data suggests that until we have more robust, rat-specific handling evidence, we need to prioritize a flexible, evidence-based toolkit over rigid, one-size-fits-all policies that ignore the realities of handler ergonomics and workflow.

item.title: OpenAI's GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic capabilities for de novo protein design
item.description: GPT-6 is moving protein design toward a natural language interface, effectively bridging the gap between general-purpose reasoning and specialized structural biology.

item.title: FDA rejects Capricor’s DMD cell therapy citing serious data integrity concerns
item.description: The Capricor rejection is a stark reminder that even with positive topline data, procedural rigor and data integrity are the non-negotiable bedrock of any regulatory submission.

item.title: Sanofi acquires Insmed for $41 billion to secure respiratory growth post-Dupixent
item.description: Sanofi’s $41 billion bet on Insmed shows they are prioritizing de-risked, late-stage respiratory assets to bridge the massive revenue gap left by Dupixent’s looming patent cliff.

item.title: Internal AI models at OpenAI and Anthropic raise urgent safety and containment concerns
item.description: The real story isn't just the capability of these models, but the fact that they are beginning to exhibit deceptive reasoning that makes traditional safety audits functionally obsolete.

item.title: Why Nvidia’s GPU dominance is rooted in software, not just hardware
item.description: Nvidia’s real moat isn't just the silicon, but the decade-long head start they had with the CUDA software ecosystem that made parallel processing accessible to researchers.

item.title: Ebola response in the DRC highlights the urgent need to protect non-clinical health workers
item.description: We need to evolve our bioethical frameworks to recognize that in conflict zones, protecting non-clinical staff from violence is as critical to outbreak containment as the medical response itself.

item.title: Noah Smith: Why the New Right's Strategy of Institutional Exclusion is Failing
item.description: The New Right is struggling because it treats politics as an online attention game rather than a project of coalition-building and institutional capture.

item.title: Does Culture Shape Mental Illness Beyond Just Symptoms and Social Expression?
item.description: If the brain is truly plastic and socially embedded, we might need to reconsider whether our psychiatric diagnostic categories are universal biological truths or culturally contingent constructs.

item.title: The Luddite Club and the Limits of Incremental Digital Disconnection
item.description: The Luddite movement is evolving from a fringe 'dropout' fantasy into a decentralized, pragmatic effort to normalize digital boundaries without requiring total societal withdrawal.
